Relevance & filters

Relevance

Readfine scores how well an article matches what you follow, and can sort and filter by it.

How scoring works

Basic relevance reads the title and the opening of every article that arrives and looks for your terms in it. It needs no API key. AI scoring rates labeled articles with a model and is noticeably more accurate, but it needs an API key.

Your terms

Unsaved changes. Save relevance settings at the bottom of the page to keep them.

Tips for terms

Separate terms with commas, semicolons or new lines. A term can be several words, such as urban cycling : an article with more of them scores higher, and they don't have to stand together. Related forms are found too ( cycling also finds cyclist ), and a translation is simply another term. Specific beats general: health on its own matches almost everything. How matching works

2 terms. Saving rescores the last 7 days of unread articles shortly. New articles are scored as they arrive.

Checking how your terms did…

Basic relevance

Runs on everything that arrives, from the title and the first 300 characters, with no API key and no cost. It is a weaker signal than AI scoring: it matches words, so it cannot tell that a report from the Tour de France is about cycling unless one of your terms appears in it. Measured against what people actually read, it ranks clearly better than plain date order and clearly worse than the AI score.

Display

Shows the relevance score: the AI score where an article has one, the basic score otherwise. A basic score is marked with ~ , since a word-match 70 is rare where an AI 70 is common. Catch me up and filters on AI, else basic use the same number.

Filters

Filters run on new articles as they arrive: when the conditions match, the actions apply automatically (add a label, mark as read, star, archive). Learn more .
